meta.description: Decides how to preprocess plasma cfDNA sequencing data so recoverable signal survives, including library-aware fragment interpretation, simplex or duplex UMI consensus with fgbio, safe alignment and filtering order, and fragment-size QC.

scientific_integrity.detail: All six DOI identifiers resolve to the cited primary publications, quantitative claims are attributed, and no output fabricates clinical or analytical performance.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill stays within preprocessing and analytical interpretation, requires assay-specific validation, and makes no patient-specific diagnostic or treatment recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: Live evidence confirms the required UMI extraction, paired FASTQ alignment and metadata zipper, template-coordinate grouping, consensus realignment, query-grouped filtering, and final coordinate sort/index topology. Duplex and chemistry guidance is explicitly assay-conditional.

code_usability.detail: Every accessible runnable surface executed in the pinned environment. Four independent workflows and all six shipped tests completed, including ten consecutive end-to-end calls.

functional_suitability.note: The skill covers the promised library-choice, UMI consensus, fragment-preservation, and insert-size QC use cases with executable and documented routes.

reliability.note: Input domains and topology are validated, subprocess failures propagate, and reruns are stable; failed external-tool runs can leave diagnostic intermediate files for the caller to inspect or remove.

performance_context.note: The core file routes detail into focused references and the executable chain avoids redundant scientific stages.

agent_usability.note: The decision table, required order, validation rules, failure modes, and reporting checklist are explicit; external tools still report their native diagnostics.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger examples, readable scenario guidance, and literal path support make the skill usable without weakening scientific input checks.

security.note: No credentials or sensitive values are embedded, all process launches are argv-only, user paths remain literal, and no eval, exec, or shell=True surface exists.

maintainability.note: Responsibilities are split across one importable module and focused references, with a six-test live regression suite; tool-version semantics still require periodic live verification as documented.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, routed detail, stable return types, idempotent reruns, explicit stop conditions, and composable functions are strong; run-summary assembly remains the invoking agent's responsibility.

inputs.label: Public cfDNA insert-size QC
inputs.note: Two independent calls returned identical public-BAM values and explicit filter counts plus interpretation context.

assertions.text: The public output reports observation count, mode, median, 90-150 bp fraction, and greater-than-250 bp fraction.
assertions.note: It reports n=2819, mode=96, median=123, short fraction=0.64349059950337, and long fraction=0.0.

assertions.text: The accepted population enforces primary, proper-pair, PF, nonduplicate, positive-template-length records.
assertions.note: The result provides overlapping counts for unmapped, improper, secondary, supplementary, duplicate, QC-fail, nonpositive, and over-bound records.

assertions.text: Repeated execution on the same BAM is deterministic.
assertions.note: The two complete result dictionaries are identical.

assertions.text: A fresh alternate maximum-size case changes the population coherently.
assertions.note: max_size=150 accepts 2190 records, reports 630 over-bound records, and yields a 0.828310502283105 short fraction.

assertions.text: The output preserves scientific interpretation boundaries.
assertions.note: It names library chemistry, collection and plasma processing, and physical or in-silico size selection as required context.

inputs.label: Simplex UMI consensus wrapper
inputs.note: A fresh full-stack simplex run produced four filtered coordinate-sorted consensus records and a valid index.

assertions.text: Each molecular UMI segment is mapped to a distinct tag while combined RX is retained.
assertions.note: All 32 extracted records carry RX, ZA, and ZB.

assertions.text: The uBAM is query-grouped, converted to paired FASTQ, aligned with BWA, and zipped to restore metadata.
assertions.note: Captured argv shows samtools fastq -T RX,ZA,ZB, bwa mem -C -p, and ZipperBams; the first zipped BAM retains all three tags on 32 records.

assertions.text: Simplex processing uses adjacency grouping and molecular consensus.
assertions.note: Captured commands use GroupReadsByUmi --strategy adjacency and CallMolecularConsensusReads; grouped MI is present on 32 records.

assertions.text: Consensus filtering receives queryname-sorted mapped consensus reads.
assertions.note: The filter input and output headers declare queryname order.

assertions.text: The final simplex BAM is useful and readable by downstream tools.
assertions.note: The final BAM has four records, coordinate order, an index, RX and MI tags, and samtools quickcheck return code 0.

inputs.label: Reciprocal duplex UMI consensus wrapper
inputs.note: Two independent duplex executions each emitted two true-duplex consensus records with identical structural results.

assertions.text: Reciprocal duplex UMIs retain RX, ZA, and ZB through extraction and the first metadata zipper.
assertions.note: Both duplex runs preserve all three tags on all 32 raw-family records.

assertions.text: Duplex processing uses paired grouping and the duplex consensus caller.
assertions.note: Captured commands use GroupReadsByUmi --strategy paired and CallDuplexConsensusReads.

assertions.text: The duplex filter enforces the documented total and two-strand threshold after realignment.
assertions.note: Captured argv uses FilterConsensusReads --min-reads 2 1 1 on queryname-sorted mapped consensus.

assertions.text: Two fresh duplex executions are structurally deterministic.
assertions.note: Each run accepts 32 grouped records and emits two final consensus records with the same stage counts and sort orders.

assertions.text: Final duplex output is coordinate-sorted, indexed, nonempty, and parseable.
assertions.note: Both final BAMs contain two records, have coordinate order and indexes, and pass samtools quickcheck.

inputs.label: QC flags, bounds, and empty BAM
inputs.note: Flag policy, invalid parameter bounds, empty input, and alternate cutoff behavior all match the documented contract.

assertions.text: Secondary, supplementary, duplicate, and QC-fail records are excluded and counted.
assertions.note: The five-record fixture accepts one record and reports one record in each named flag category.

assertions.text: Invalid maximum-size values fail with specific domain errors.
assertions.note: 0 and -1 raise ValueError; True and 1.5 raise TypeError with specific messages.

assertions.text: An empty BAM returns a stable typed zero summary rather than crashing or fabricating observations.
assertions.note: All numeric outputs and filter counts are zero and interpretation_context remains present.

assertions.text: Filter counts are explicitly documented as overlapping reasons rather than a false partition.
assertions.note: The function docstring states the overlapping-count contract and the returned fields follow it.

assertions.text: No output turns preprocessing QC into a patient-specific clinical conclusion.
assertions.note: The output is an analytical summary with required assay context and no diagnosis or treatment claim.

inputs.label: Literal metacharacter paths and ten-call stability
inputs.note: A full metacharacter-path workflow and the separate six-test live suite completed with no side effect or stability failure.

assertions.text: Input, reference, intermediate, and output paths with spaces and shell metacharacters remain literal argv values.
assertions.note: The path containing spaces, semicolon, dollar sign, and brackets completed and captured commands preserve each full path as one argument.

assertions.text: No shell command execution or code-evaluation surface is present.
assertions.note: AST inspection finds zero shell=True, eval, or exec calls, and the metacharacter run creates no shell side-effect path.

assertions.text: The metacharacter workflow produces a useful final BAM.
assertions.note: It contains four coordinate-sorted records, has an index, and passes samtools quickcheck.

assertions.text: Ten consecutive complete calls meet the stability gate.
assertions.note: The shipped live suite executes ten calls and asserts an identical four-record count on every call; the full suite exits 0 with no skips.

assertions.text: The executable and documentation retain assay-conditional scientific boundaries.
assertions.note: Guidance requires recovery, molecular depth, background, targets, pre-analytics, caller, and validated LoD context, and all six cited DOI identifiers resolve.

key_strengths: The executable preserves the required cfDNA UMI topology from per-segment tag extraction through consensus realignment and filtering.
All process execution is argv-only and literal-path regressions cover spaces and multiple shell metacharacters.
Fragment QC exposes the selected population, overlapping exclusion counts, parameter errors, and assay interpretation context.
The scientific guidance separates method capability from achieved assay performance and routes quantitative claims to six resolvable primary references.
